INSTRUCTIONS TO CREDIT UNION:  Please fill out any column that the header of the column is in GREEN.  Please fill these out to the best of your ability.  

The first row in this spreadsheet will give you HELP on what the Column should have entered into it.  If you need further assistance, please reach out to the Project Manager assigned to your conversion

column7: Enter an alphanumeric (up to 4 characters) code and a description for this product type. Since the description of the product is used throughout the system, it is important the description is unique and allows for easy identification of the account by the user.

column13: Enter the Base Rate or Interest Rate for the loan product. (This will be used to determine what margin is applied to the base rate if using Risk Based Lending (RBL).  If not using RBL, this is the rate that will be assigned to a new loan application at the time of modeling the loan.  This rate can be changed at any time on a loan application.

column20: Enter the maximum number of months the next due date will be allowed to advance.  The next due date will not advance into the future more than this number of months from the current date.  This value should be "1" for interest only payment line of credit loans. A value of "0" will allow the due date to be advanced into the future an unlimited number of months.

column23: Enter the general ledger account used for posting interest transactions on loans with this Loan Product, or click the Look button to select an account.
column24: Enter the share account type to be used for deposits of escrow amount on payments for loans associated to this loan product, or use the Look button to select an account type. Leave this field blank if the loan product has no associated escrow.
column25:
Enter the Payment Posting Priority for this loan product.  Values for this are Fees, Interest, Principal and Escrow and can fall in any order.  

(In the drop down FIPE would be Fees, Interest, Principal and Escrow ; IFPE would be for Interest, Fees, Principal and Escrow...etc)
column26:
Check this box if the payment amount applied plus the Partial Payment Amount is greater than the scheduled loan payment amount and the amount over the scheduled loan payment should be applied to late fees. 

NOTE: If Principal is slotted first, all principal due will be taken before fees will be paid.
column27:
Select the code used to designate the method used to Recalculate The Payment amount on LOC loans:

0 =  not a LOC loan
1 =  payment will be recalculated manually
2 =  $X per $Y of outstanding loan balance (e.g. $5.00 per $100.00)
3 =  % of outstanding loan balance (e.g. if 5% and loan balance = $7500.00, then payment = $375.00)
4 =  uses original loan term and outstanding loan balance to recalculate payment. The original loan date and first payment date are also used in the calculation.
5 =  uses remaining term and outstanding loan balance to recalculate payment. The remaining term is calculated from the current loan due date to the original maturity date of the loan. The original loan date and first payment date are also used in the calculation.
6 =  interest only payment calculations.

Select Yes if loan payments can only bump the 'Due Date' on the loan one frequency beyond the current 'Due Date' at the time of each payment.

Note: For example, payments on delinquent loans could bump the 'Due Date' multiple frequencies to bring the loan current, but not more than 1 frequency beyond the current 'Due Date'. The Bump Due Date Once flag takes priority over the Bump Max Months value.

column53:
Select the NCUA method used to calculate delinquency:

Method D - delinquent amount = ((scheduled payment amount * # of delinquent installments) - partial payment amount)

Method B - compares the loan balance to the loan's amortization schedule to determine the expected loan balance at a given point in time to determine delinquent amount.

 (Default is D)
column54: Enter the number of delinquent days lapsed prior to marking loans for collection.
column55: Enter the number of delinquent days lapsed before loans with this Loan Type are considered past due.  If this is a line of credit loan product, this field is also used to determine if loan advances are allowed.  If the loan due date plus the loan product "past due days" is less than the current date, loan advances are not allowed for member transactions, and batch processes (Share Draft processing, ACH processing, ATM processing).
column56: Enter the number of delinquent days lapsed before a yellow message prompt is given to the user to inform them the member has delinquent loans. This prompt will occur during member inquiries and member transactions. The user record must have the "Delinquent Alert Flag" set to true in order to receive these warning messages. Delinquent credit cards will also be included in the message.
column57: Enter the number of delinquent days lapsed before a reminder notice is generated.
column58: Enter the number of delinquent days lapsed before a red message prompt is given to the user to inform them the member has seriously delinquent loans and authorization will be required to perform transactions. This prompt will occur during member inquiries and member transactions. While processing a member transaction, the delinquent override pop-up box will appear requiring an override for any transaction to be performed. Delinquent credit cards will also be included in the message.
